title: A Drop of Relief

patient.name: Mdm Wong Siok Hwa
patient.presenting_complaint: Gritty, burning sensation in both eyes, worse by the end of the day

history.hpc: Mdm Wong has been diagnosed with bilateral dry eye disease today after assessment by the doctor, who has prescribed preservative-free artificial tears to be used four times a day in both eyes. She has used eye drops before for conjunctivitis many years ago but never on a regular daily basis. She mentions she finds it awkward to instil drops without help and often ends up with the drop running down her cheek.
history.pmhx: Bilateral dry eye disease (newly characterised today). Hypertension, well-controlled. No diabetes. No previous eye surgery.
history.allergies: No drug allergy recorded on file.
medications: Preservative-free artificial tears, both eyes, 4 times a day — newly prescribed today
history.social_hx: Lives with husband. Spends a lot of time reading and watching TV. Uses an electric fan at home which she says may dry her eyes further.

examination_findings.fundus: Not assessed at this stage — reviewed by doctor

investigations.note: VA and IOP already completed by clinical staff before this education session. This session focuses on eye drop instillation technique for newly prescribed artificial tears.

diagnosis: Patient education session for self-administered preservative-free artificial tears, four times daily, both eyes. Mdm Wong has minimal prior experience with regular drop instillation. Education goal: patient demonstrates correct single-handed technique for both eyes by end of session.

immediate: Confirm the prescribed medication (preservative-free artificial tears), the eye(s) to be treated (both), and the frequency (four times a day) with the patient before starting
Check for any known allergies to eye drop ingredients or preservatives
Explain the purpose simply: 'These drops add moisture to your eyes to relieve the gritty, burning feeling. Using them regularly through the day will help keep your eyes comfortable.'
Demonstrate the technique step by step using a demo or capped bottle:
Step 1 — Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water
Step 2 — Tilt the head back slightly or sit in a reclined position
Step 3 — Gently pull the lower eyelid down with one finger to form a small pocket
Step 4 — Look up and away from the bottle tip
Step 5 — Hold the bottle close to the eye without touching the eye, lashes, or lid
Step 6 — Squeeze gently to release one drop into the lower pocket
Step 7 — Close the eye gently for a few seconds, blot any excess from the cheek with a clean tissue
Have Mdm Wong practise the technique on both eyes while you observe, giving constructive feedback
If preservative-free single-use vials are prescribed, show how to open, use once, and discard the vial — do not reuse
follow_up: Confirm Mdm Wong can demonstrate the technique correctly on both eyes before she leaves
If she is using single-use vials, confirm she understands not to reuse or store opened vials
Advise her to call the clinic if she continues to have difficulty after trying at home
patient_education: Use the drops four times a day as prescribed, even if symptoms improve, unless told otherwise by the doctor
If using single-dose preservative-free vials, discard each vial after one use — do not save it for later
Wait at least 5 minutes between different eye drops if she is prescribed more than one type
Reducing direct exposure to fans or air-conditioning vents may help reduce dryness symptoms

key_points: Confirms the correct medication, eye(s), and frequency before starting the education session
Checks for known drug or preservative allergies
Identifies the patient's limited prior experience with regular drop instillation
Asks about the patient's home environment factors relevant to dry eye (e.g., fan use) without making a clinical judgement
Demonstrates the instillation technique step-by-step before asking the patient to practise
Observes the patient practise on both eyes and gives specific feedback
If single-use vials are involved, demonstrates correct opening, one-time use, and disposal
Checks the patient's understanding using teach-back
Recognises that correct technique is essential for the drops to be effective and comfortable
Identifies that running drops down the cheek means an incomplete dose was delivered
Does not provide a clinical diagnosis beyond what the doctor has already told the patient
Understands that consistent four-times-daily use is part of managing dry eye symptoms
Uses teach-back: patient demonstrates the technique on both eyes, not just listens
Covers practical tips for single-handed instillation appropriate for an independent older adult
Explains storage/use rules for single-use preservative-free vials if applicable
Provides relevant lifestyle advice (e.g., reducing fan exposure) as general comfort tips, not medical instructions
